title: Magnetic Properties of High-Entropy Alloy FeCoNiTi

recollection.starting_material: Guess: equiatomic Fe, Co, Ni, and Ti elemental powders consolidated into an alloy
recollection.intervention: Guess: vacuum arc melting followed by homogenization annealing and optionally mechanical milling
recollection.structure: Guess: single‐phase body‐centered cubic (BCC) solid solution with some B2 ordering tendencies
recollection.mechanism: Guess: lattice distortion from Ti addition enhances exchange interactions and magnetocrystalline anisotropy, stabilizing ferromagnetism
recollection.results: Guess: room‐temperature saturation magnetization ≈110 emu/g, coercivity ≈80 Oe, and Curie temperature ≈620 K

score.note: The recollection partially identifies arc melting, but misses rapid quenching on a water-cooled Cu hearth and the C14-dominant comparison alloy, while adding unsupported annealing/milling. The claimed single-phase BCC/B2 structure contradicts the actual fcc+C14 dual-phase structure. The proposed lattice-distortion mechanism is incorrect, and all cited magnetic values differ substantially from the reported transitions (1084, 214, and 168 K) and coercivity (667 Oe at 400 K).
